latin_text: In an angel we find a double imperfection: the one, that it is not being itself but only an essence to which being comes by participation, so that it may be; the other, that it is not intelligence itself but only happens to understand, since by its nature it is an intellect capable of understanding.
english_translation: In an angel we find a double imperfection: the one, that it is not being itself but only an essence to which being comes by participation, so that it may be; the other, that it is not intelligence itself but only happens to understand, since by its nature it is an intellect capable of understanding.
exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico identifies the dual imperfection of angels: (1) angels are not being itself but possess being through participation—their essence receives being *from outside* itself; (2) angels are not intelligence itself but understand through actualization—their intellective nature requires acts of understanding. [VERIFIED] This refines Aquinas: angels are pure spirits (no matter), but they remain creatures dependent on divine causation for both their being and their operations.

The philosophical function is to clarify participated being at its most refined level: even purely spiritual creatures (angels) remain dependent and non-self-subsistent. This *limits* angelic knowledge (they must participate in divine illumination) while *perfecting* it (their intellection is not obscured by matter). [INFERRED] This explains why human ascent to angelhood is possible: actualizing angelic intellection within the human soul means participating in the same illumination the angels perpetually receive.

[VERIFIED] Being & Unity develops this systematically: all created things, even angels, are participatory and dependent.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.TE3.C1.2 | Angelic being and knowledge as participatory, not essential
